question: How does the choice of language model used to calculate surprisal affect comparisons of linguistic diversity between human and machine-generated image captions?
reference_answer: With a caption-trained n-gram language model, human captions have roughly twice the surprisal variance of model captions. Using a general-language model to rescore the same captions reverses this pattern, showing that diversity evaluations should use several scorers.
gold_titles: Surprisal reveals diversity gaps in image captioning and different scorers change the story

question: How much can audio token sequences be compressed before the LLM backbone while preserving performance on speech tasks?
reference_answer: The experiments show that compressed LALMs can reduce the input audio token count up to three times while achieving performance close to frame-level LALMs on automatic speech recognition and speech-to-speech translation.
gold_titles: Towards Audio Token Compression in Large Audio Language Models

question: How does LAPA use videos without robot action labels to pretrain a VLA model, and how are the learned actions connected to robot controls?
reference_answer: It first learns discrete latent actions between image frames using an action quantization model with a VQ-VAE-based objective, then trains a latent VLA model to predict those actions from observations and task descriptions. Finally, it fine-tunes the VLA on a small amount of robot manipulation data to map latent actions to robot actions.
gold_titles: Latent Action Pretraining from Videos

question: On an embedded robot, deploying separate deep models for depth estimation, object detection, and semantic segmentation wastes computation and memory — is there a way to share one feature extractor across all of these tasks in parallel, and can each task's update rate still be tuned independently?
reference_answer: The proposed modular framework runs a shared foundation model backbone (DINOv2 in the example) whose image representations are reused by several specialized task heads executing in parallel, avoiding redundant feature extraction and GPU–CPU memory transfers while allowing per-task inference frequencies to be adjusted dynamically at runtime with a constant memory footprint on CUDA MPS. The example implementation achieves up to 3x speedup over sequential execution and end-to-end real-time performance at ≥50 Hz on NVIDIA Jetson Orin AGX for TensorRT-optimized models.
gold_titles: Visual Perception Engine: Fast and Flexible Multi-Head Inference for Robotic Vision Tasks

question: How can lip-movement cues and automatically transcribed multilingual recordings be used to improve speech recognition in noisy conditions, and what performance gains have been reported?
reference_answer: A multilingual model combines audio and visual inputs and expands training data for six languages using automatic transcriptions of unlabelled VoxCeleb2 and AVSpeech recordings. It achieves 0.8% WER on LRS3 and an absolute average-WER reduction of 11.9% over the original MuAViC baseline.
gold_titles: Multilingual Audio-Visual Speech Recognition with Hybrid CTC/RNN-T Fast Conformer

question: If the controller for a robot arm doing high-dimensional manipulation were built from spiking neurons instead of standard artificial neural networks, how much energy could actually be saved, and does the motion accuracy hold up?
reference_answer: On the Isaac Gym PixMC manipulation benchmark, using a spiking-network actor for the Franka arm delivered energy savings of up to 96.10% over an equivalent artificial neural network while maintaining comparable control performance. The learned policies tracked commanded finger positions with minimal deviation and kept a stable target height during pick-and-place operations.
gold_titles: Population-Coded Spiking Neural Networks for High-Dimensional Robotic Control

question: Why do today's large generative models work so well for building representations of individual users from posts, preferences and interaction networks, and how are they combined with classical text and graph mining pipelines?
reference_answer: Because these models show superior performance at generating, understanding, and even reasoning over text, they can capture a user's profile, preference, and personality from user-generated content. Surveyed solutions integrate them with text-based and graph-based methods in different ways, covering applications such as recommendation, education, and healthcare, and the work also identifies remaining challenges and future directions.
gold_titles: User Modeling in the Era of Large Language Models: Current Research and Future Directions

question: How do input modality, problem difficulty, and response format affect whether an LLM benefits more from generalizing patterns or explicitly forming and testing logical explanations?
reference_answer: Abductive and deductive reasoning pipelines generally perform better on visual or symbolic inputs and harder tasks, while inductive reasoning is competitive on textual inputs and easier problems. Response format can reverse this advantage, with induction sometimes outperforming the other approaches in free-text rule execution.
gold_titles: LogiDynamics: Unraveling the Dynamics of Inductive, Abductive and Deductive Logical Inferences in LLM Reasoning

question: How can reaction data be extracted from a chemistry document when the relevant information is distributed across different parts of the publication?
reference_answer: The approach first extracts information from individual modalities such as text, tables, and figures using specialized neural models, then integrates those results with chemistry-informed algorithms to produce a final list of reactions at the document level.
gold_titles: OpenChemIE: An Information Extraction Toolkit For Chemistry Literature

question: How does Pistis-RAG learn from feedback that applies to an entire list of retrieved inputs, and what accuracy gains does it report?
reference_answer: Pistis-RAG treats feedback such as copy, regenerate, or dislike as a Listwide Labels Learning-to-Rank task and uses it to improve content ranking and generation quality. It reports accuracy increases of 6.06% on English MMLU and 7.08% on Chinese C-EVAL relative to baseline RAG.
gold_titles: Pistis-RAG: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Human Feedback

question: When the Schrödinger bridge construction is recast in the style of a variational autoencoder, which inequality is used to justify the decomposition, and what terms does the resulting training objective consist of?
reference_answer: The data processing inequality is the key ingredient: interpreting these bridge-based generators as a generalization of variational autoencoders yields an objective function that splits into two parts, a prior loss and a drift matching term.
gold_titles: Sch\"odinger Bridge Type Diffusion Models as an Extension of Variational Autoencoders

question: How can the assumption that outcomes change smoothly over time help train survival models on large longitudinal datasets with long observation sequences?
reference_answer: It provides a stable training signal that captures long-term temporal relationships and supports reliable updates during end-to-end training. Experiments show improved training stability and performance exceeding benchmarks on datasets with long sequences.
gold_titles: Deep End-to-End Survival Analysis with Temporal Consistency

question: For subjective tasks, do LLM sampling and log-probability methods with tuned parameters yield opinion distributions that match people better than simply prompting the model directly?
reference_answer: Yes — an empirical comparison of three approaches found that sampling and log-probability methods with simple parameter adjustments returned better aligned outputs than direct prompting on subjective tasks. The study also cautions that assuming models reflect human opinions may itself be limiting, highlighting the need for further research into how human subjectivity affects model uncertainty.
gold_titles: Understanding The Effect Of Temperature On Alignment With Human Opinions

question: Can right-to-left autoregressive training improve language model performance on multiple-choice benchmarks compared with left-to-right training, and what factors may explain the difference?
reference_answer: Experiments across models with 2B–8B parameters and various training datasets show that right-to-left models can significantly outperform left-to-right models on multiple-choice benchmarks involving logical reasoning, commonsense understanding, and truthfulness assessment. The performance difference may be linked to calibration, computability, and directional conditional entropy.
gold_titles: What Makes the Preferred Thinking Direction for LLMs in Multiple-choice Questions?

question: Why might foundation models need to use non-Euclidean geometries, and what integration strategies are proposed?
reference_answer: Real-world data often has structures such as multi-way relationships, hierarchies, symmetries, and non-isotropic scaling that are difficult to capture in Euclidean spaces; adopting non-Euclidean geometries could help foundation models leverage these structures and sustain scaling. Proposed strategies include fine-tuning, training from scratch, and hybrid approaches.
gold_titles: Position: Beyond Euclidean -- Foundation Models Should Embrace Non-Euclidean Geometries

question: How can pre-trained LLMs be adapted to predict unsteady fluid dynamics while accounting for complex spatial geometries and temporal evolution?
reference_answer: FLUID-LLM combines pre-trained LLMs with spatiotemporal-aware encoding, leveraging their temporal autoregressive abilities alongside spatial-aware layers. Evaluations on standard benchmarks show significant performance improvements across various fluid datasets.
gold_titles: FLUID-LLM: Learning Computational Fluid Dynamics with Spatiotemporal-aware Large Language Models

question: On the CLadder benchmark, does a setup in which one model proposes a causal inference while another critiques its logic improve accuracy on counterfactual questions, and by how much for DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen3?
reference_answer: Yes. Multi-agent debate raised DeepSeek-R1's overall accuracy from 78.03% to 87.45% and its counterfactual accuracy from 67.94% to 80.04%, while Qwen3's overall accuracy rose from 84.16% to 89.41% and its counterfactual accuracy from 71.53% to 80.35%, so even the stronger model benefits from debate with a weaker one.
gold_titles: CRAwDAD: Causal Reasoning Augmentation with Dual-Agent Debate

question: How can a learned docking model incorporate molecular geometry and whole-ligand information to improve predicted binding poses?
reference_answer: An equivariant transformer can fuse ligand graph-level features and learn protein and ligand representations while accounting for their 3D spatial information. Iterative optimization using a predicted distance matrix then refines ligand poses, achieving state-of-the-art performance on real datasets.
gold_titles: ETDock: A Novel Equivariant Transformer for Protein-Ligand Docking

question: What timescales emerge in the training dynamics of wide two-layer neural networks when analyzed with dynamical mean field theory, and how do they separate the feature learning stage from the overfitting regime?
reference_answer: For large network width m and large samples per input dimension n/d, the training dynamics exhibits a separation of timescales, with a slow time scale associated with growth in the network's Gaussian/Rademacher complexity and an inductive bias toward small complexity when the initialization is sufficiently small-complexity. This leads to a dynamical decoupling between feature learning and overfitting regimes, plus a non-monotone behavior of the test error at large times corresponding to a "feature unlearning" regime.
gold_titles: Dynamical Decoupling of Generalization and Overfitting in Large Two-Layer Networks

question: When a predictor is already close to calibrated in a smooth, perturbation-insensitive sense, can it be converted into reliable inputs for an optimizing decision-maker, and how much calibration quality is lost in the process?
reference_answer: Post-processing an online predictor with epsilon distance to calibration yields O(sqrt(epsilon)) ECE and CDL, which is asymptotically optimal for that route, though still worse than algorithms that directly optimize ECE and CDL.
gold_titles: Smooth Calibration and Decision Making

question: How can state abstraction reduce the difficulty of OPE in high-cardinality state spaces, and what consistency guarantees hold for estimators using the resulting representations?
reference_answer: An iterative procedure sequentially projects the original state space into smaller spaces, producing a deeply-abstracted state that substantially simplifies the sample complexity of OPE arising from high cardinality. Various OPE estimators are proved to be Fisher consistent when applied to the proposed abstract state spaces.
gold_titles: Off-policy Evaluation with Deeply-abstracted States

question: What new review-level task is introduced to identify all ABSA constituents across complete reviews, and how are its datasets expanded to address previous evaluation limitations?
reference_answer: The Review-Level Opinion Aspect Sentiment Target (ROAST) task identifies every ABSA constituent at the review level. Its datasets are extended to include low-resource languages, multiple languages, and diverse topics.
gold_titles: ROAST: Review-level Opinion Aspect Sentiment Target Joint Detection for ABSA

question: How can combining conventional video with event-camera data improve recognition of everyday actions under poor lighting or rapid motion, and what benchmark supports this research?
reference_answer: The HARDVS 2.0 benchmark contains 300 categories of real-world actions and 107,646 paired videos covering challenging scenarios. The proposed approach fuses RGB and event features and achieves strong performance, demonstrating effectiveness and robustness.
gold_titles: Human Activity Recognition using RGB-Event based Sensors: A Multi-modal Heat Conduction Model and A Benchmark Dataset

question: Most semi-supervised approaches for segmenting medical scans lean on consistency regularization and pseudo-labels, ignoring semantic relationships that could transfer across clinical sites and imaging modalities. Is there a way to place a teacher and a student network in a shared feature space so the teacher's knowledge is transferred without explicitly generating synthetic training data?
reference_answer: The proposed approach aligns domain-invariant semantics via cross-domain distribution matching while preserving intra-domain structure, and adaptively augments teacher features toward the student's semantics using a lightweight memory module, so the semantic transformation occurs implicitly rather than through explicit data generation. The augmentation is realized as an expected transferable cross-entropy loss over the augmented teacher distribution, whose upper bound is theoretically derived and minimized during training with negligible computational overhead, and experiments on medical image datasets show it outperforms existing semi-supervised methods.
gold_titles: TransMedSeg: A Transferable Semantic Framework for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation

question: How can synthetic text generation be guided to stay relevant to a target domain while avoiding repetition of existing examples?
reference_answer: The approach emphasizes the difference between fine-tuned and base language-model logit distributions to promote domain adherence, and uses real or synthetic examples as negative prompts to encourage diversity. Its hyperparameters control the trade-off between coherence and diversity.
gold_titles: Steering Language Generation: Harnessing Contrastive Expert Guidance and Negative Prompting for Coherent and Diverse Synthetic Data Generation

question: Can quantum layers layered onto a classical graph-based neural network offer a competitive way to predict the formation energies of perovskite materials compared with purely classical machine learning approaches?
reference_answer: The authors built a gradient-free hybrid quantum-classical convolutional graph neural network and found its predictive performance on perovskite formation energies was competitive with both a purely classical convolutional graph neural network and classical algorithms such as XGBoost. They conclude that quantum feature encoding and parametric quantum circuits offer a promising path toward substantial improvements of complex graph neural network models.
gold_titles: Hybrid Quantum Graph Neural Network for Molecular Property Prediction

question: How can a web agent better understand which page elements are relevant to its current instruction when the underlying markup alone lacks task-specific cues?
reference_answer: It can enrich each HTML element by combining its textual information with the visual appearance and bounding box of the corresponding region in the page screenshot, along with nearby elements that are likely related to the task. This produces more informative element representations that improve action selection across different tasks, websites, and domains.
gold_titles: Dual-View Visual Contextualization for Web Navigation

question: Which deep learning architecture achieved the strongest proton rejection for ECAL shower classification, and how did its advantage compare between Monte Carlo and ISS data?
reference_answer: The Convolutional vision Transformer (CvT) model achieved more than 5 times the proton rejection power of the other deep learning models for MC events and more than 2.5 times for ISS data.
gold_titles: A Comparison of Deep Learning Models for Proton Background Rejection with the AMS Electromagnetic Calorimeter

question: How does the proposed approach make SHAP feature-importance results more understandable to nontechnical users?
reference_answer: It integrates SHAP with OpenAI's GPT to generate contextualized textual explanations guided by feature aliases, descriptions, and additional background. In a healthcare case study, users perceived these explanations as more understandable and contextually appropriate than visual-only outputs.
gold_titles: ContextualSHAP : Enhancing SHAP Explanations Through Contextual Language Generation

question: How can sparse regression and a recurrent convolutional neural network be combined to identify governing wave equations with spatially varying coefficients from noisy, low-resolution observations?
reference_answer: A hybrid framework alternates between a discovery phase, which uses sparse regression to preliminarily identify governing equations, and an embedding phase, which uses a recurrent convolutional neural network to refine functional terms and coefficients. Numerical experiments across elastic/viscoelastic and homogeneous/inhomogeneous media demonstrate robustness and accuracy under high noise and limited spatial and temporal data.
gold_titles: Discovery and inversion of the viscoelastic wave equation in inhomogeneous media

question: Which pre-trained Transformer architectures were evaluated for predicting MeSH publication types from MEDLINE citation metadata, and what classifier formulations were compared?
reference_answer: BERT and DistilBERT were evaluated, comparing monolithic multi-label classifiers against ensembles of binary classifiers. The results showed that these Transformer models could significantly improve publication type tagging accuracy.
gold_titles: Enhancing Automatic PT Tagging for MEDLINE Citations Using Transformer-Based Models

question: How can a retrieval system improve the chance of finding the right document passage when a user's query does not closely match the wording of the original text?
reference_answer: The approach decomposes each chunk into atomic statements and generates synthetic questions over those statements, then retrieves by matching the user query to those questions. This yields higher chunk recall than retrieving with the original chunks, and synthetic questions over the atoms improve recall further.
gold_titles: Question-Based Retrieval using Atomic Units for Enterprise RAG

question: Why can entropy minimization become unstable when adapting a pretrained classifier one test sample at a time, and how does the proposed robust framework address unreliable samples without simply discarding them?
reference_answer: Entropy minimization in online fully-test-time adaptation is unstable in single-sample settings and can collapse to degenerate solutions, with noisy or unreliable samples identified as a key cause. The framework instead uses a robust, self-paced-inspired loss that down-weights unreliable samples while avoiding the update bias and slow adaptation caused by ignoring them entirely.
gold_titles: REALM: Robust Entropy Adaptive Loss Minimization for Improved Single-Sample Test-Time Adaptation

question: For large Conformer-based speech recognition systems, is it feasible to train from scratch with weight matrices constrained to low rank, and which parts of the architecture tolerate heavy rank reduction without hurting accuracy?
reference_answer: Yes: with SVD-based initialization and a linear layer-wise rank assignment, training from scratch with reduced-rank weights reaches parity with full-rank training while cutting the parameter count by at least 2x and speeding up training by 1.3x for ASR and 1.15x for AVSR. Applying the low-rank constraint only to the attention modules can even improve performance at a 12% rank reduction, whereas feed-forward layers start to degrade with a moderate 50% rank reduction.
gold_titles: Full-Rank No More: Low-Rank Weight Training for Modern Speech Recognition Models

question: How does the proposed framework estimate uncertainty in generative models across different modalities, and what evidence supports its usefulness?
reference_answer: It derives kernel-based variance and entropy from a bias-variance-covariance decomposition, with unbiased and consistent estimators requiring only generated samples rather than access to the underlying model. Experiments across image, audio, and language generation show that kernel entropy predicts performance on CoQA and TriviaQA better than existing baselines and works with closed-source models.
gold_titles: A Bias-Variance-Covariance Decomposition of Kernel Scores for Generative Models

question: How can attenuation maps be generated directly from low-dose PET without an additional CT scan, and what role can population-level anatomical information play?
reference_answer: A network extracts both low-resolution abstract features and fine details from low-dose PET, while a prior generator trained on a comprehensive dataset of CT-derived attenuation maps supplies additional information. Combining these components in a cascade enables iterative refinement of attenuation maps and outperforms previous baseline methods for CT-free low-count PET attenuation correction.
gold_titles: POUR-Net: A Population-Prior-Aided Over-Under-Representation Network for Low-Count PET Attenuation Map Generation

question: How can new loss functions for aligning language models with human preferences be found without relying on manually designed, theoretically motivated objectives?
reference_answer: An LLM is iteratively prompted to propose and implement new preference optimization loss functions based on previously evaluated performance metrics, leading to the discovery of previously unknown and performant algorithms. The best, called DiscoPOP, adaptively blends logistic and exponential losses and achieves state-of-the-art performance that transfers to held-out tasks.
gold_titles: Discovering Preference Optimization Algorithms with and for Large Language Models

question: How can models adapt to unfamiliar tasks in fields where large pretraining datasets are unavailable?
reference_answer: Neural memory can support adaptation to non-stationary distributions from only a few samples, while hypernetworks can learn generalizable priors and transfer them efficiently to new tasks with limited data.
gold_titles: Acquiring and Adapting Priors for Novel Tasks via Neural Meta-Architectures

question: How well can real-time crash prediction identify crashes in different areas around an intersection using connected-vehicle data?
reference_answer: The strongest models achieved 73% sensitivity within the intersection and 70% in the approach zone.
gold_titles: inTformer: A Time-Embedded Attention-Based Transformer for Crash Likelihood Prediction at Intersections Using Connected Vehicle Data

question: When parameters and computations are restricted to discrete fixed-point values with rounding error, which activation functions still let a network realize every function from fixed-point vectors to fixed-point numbers?
reference_answer: The sufficient condition is satisfied by Sigmoid, ReLU, ELU, SoftPlus, SiLU, Mish, and GELU, so networks using any of those activations can represent all fixed-point functions; even binary weights in {-1,1} suffice for practical activations. Under a mild condition on the activation (for example, that some fixed-point x satisfies σ(x)=0), the necessary and sufficient conditions coincide.
gold_titles: On Expressive Power of Quantized Neural Networks under Fixed-Point Arithmetic

question: How does MADIL use the Minimum Description Length principle for ARC tasks, and what trade-off does it show relative to LLM-based methods?
reference_answer: MADIL leverages the Minimum Description Length principle for efficient inductive learning and uses pattern-based decomposition to enable structured generalization. Its performance of 7% at ArcPrize 2024 remains below LLM-based methods, but it offers greater efficiency and interpretability.
gold_titles: MADIL: An MDL-based Framework for Efficient Program Synthesis in the ARC Benchmark

question: What approach is proposed for reliably evaluating synthetic speech that closely resembles natural human speech across languages and domains?
reference_answer: The work proposes TTSDS2, a more robust version of TTSDS, and reports that it was the only one of 16 evaluated metrics to achieve a Spearman correlation above 0.50 across every domain and subjective score. It also provides over 11,000 subjective ratings, a multilingual test-data pipeline designed to avoid data leakage, and a benchmark covering 14 languages.
gold_titles: TTSDS2: Resources and Benchmark for Evaluating Human-Quality Text to Speech Systems

question: How can gradient ascent be combined with gradient descent to improve hyperparameter robustness when unlearning information from a pre-trained LLM?
reference_answer: Integrating gradient ascent with gradient descent on in-distribution data improves hyperparameter robustness in the unlearning process.
gold_titles: Machine Unlearning of Pre-trained Large Language Models

question: What conditions allow gradient-based optimization of Transformers to reach a global minimum as both width and depth become arbitrarily large?
reference_answer: As Transformer width and depth tend to infinity, gradient flow with weight decay converges to a Wasserstein gradient flow described by a partial differential equation. With sufficiently small weight decay, it reaches a global minimum consistent with that equation's solution, under assumptions of partial homogeneity and local Lipschitz smoothness.
gold_titles: Global Convergence in Training Large-Scale Transformers

question: Is it possible to build a language model that stores text directly instead of acquiring that knowledge through training, and can what it has stored be inspected or removed afterwards?
reference_answer: Yes. The proposed architecture memorizes sequences of tokens directly in layered associative memories rather than through learning, and by design it offers transparency and the possibility of model editing, including forgetting texts. Experiments with both one-layer and multi-layer configurations demonstrated the memorization power of this design.
gold_titles: MeMo: Towards Language Models with Associative Memory Mechanisms

question: How much noise can automatically generated training labels contain while still supporting competitive deep learning classification of whole-slide biomedical images?
reference_answer: The analysis identifies 10% label noise as a level that still allows competitive whole-slide image classification models. Automatically generated labels with 2–5% noise yielded performance comparable to training with manual labels.
gold_titles: Automatic Labels are as Effective as Manual Labels in Biomedical Images Classification with Deep Learning

question: How can preference data be sampled so that reward-model training more directly supports maximizing the underlying human values, especially in iterative or online RLHF?
reference_answer: The proposed strategy samples responses by interpolating policies, explicitly aligning preference learning with maximizing the underlying oracle reward. It is theoretically optimal from optimization and statistical perspectives and performs strongly in iterative and online RLHF settings.
gold_titles: PILAF: Optimal Human Preference Sampling for Reward Modeling

question: How can researchers study detailed resource usage and execution characteristics of large-scale cluster workloads on a desktop machine without access to the original infrastructure?
reference_answer: They can use a high-fidelity simulator that parses real workload traces from a 12.5K-node Google cluster over a calendar month, revealing precise parameters for jobs, tasks, and nodes along with actual resource usage statistics.
gold_titles: AGOCS -- Accurate Google Cloud Simulator Framework

question: Is it possible to automatically derive closed-form cost functions for logic programs by having a learner guess candidate expressions for the recurrence relations that static resource analysis produces, and then verifying those candidates, and does this do better than existing automatic analyzers?
reference_answer: The approach uses sparse-linear and symbolic regression to guess a candidate closed-form function for an arbitrary constrained recurrence relation, and combines an SMT solver with a computer algebra system to check whether the candidate actually satisfies the recurrence. In a prototype integrated with CiaoPP, it outperforms state-of-the-art cost analyzers and recurrence solvers on the considered benchmarks and additionally solves recurrences that those tools cannot solve.
gold_titles: A Machine Learning-based Approach for Solving Recurrence Relations and its use in Cost Analysis of Logic Programs

question: How does FIcsR address the computational challenge of minimizing covariate shift across data fragments, and how is the resulting estimate used?
reference_answer: It derives a Fisher Information approximation to make the numerical solution tractable for an overparameterized neural network. Accumulated across fragments, this provides a global estimate of the shift remediation needed, which is incorporated as a prior in the minimization objective.
gold_titles: Mitigating covariate shift in non-colocated data with learned parameter priors

question: Why can curvature information be computationally practical for adapting pretrained models through low-rank updates?
reference_answer: The associated generalized Fisher information matrix is either low-rank or extremely small and is shown to be equivalent to the Hessian. This structure supports an efficient second-order algorithm designed to accelerate low-rank fine-tuning.
gold_titles: AdaFish: Fast low-rank parameter-efficient fine-tuning by using second-order information

question: How can an automated retinal screening pipeline be designed to remain both clinically accurate and fair across patient groups when image quality and demographic bias threaten its reliability?
reference_answer: The system combines image preprocessing, quality assessment, and specialized classification models built with ethical principles across the AI lifecycle. On 1,046 unseen patients it improved F1, accuracy, and specificity over an FDA-approved comparator while maintaining equitable performance across demographic subgroups.
gold_titles: Design and Validation of a Responsible Artificial Intelligence-based System for the Referral of Diabetic Retinopathy Patients

question: How can automated evaluation distinguish whether a language model understands broad themes versus specific details in a book-length text, and how reliable is it compared with human judgment?
reference_answer: Source texts can be organized into a three-level hierarchy of key facts, with query-focused summarization used to assess recall and faithful representation at each level. This automated evaluation achieves over 90% agreement with expert human judgments while reducing costs by up to 25 times, and reveals particular difficulties with fine-grained details.
gold_titles: Towards a Holistic and Automated Evaluation Framework for Multi-Level Comprehension of LLMs in Book-Length Contexts

question: How does the proposed melanoma diagnosis approach use non-expert feedback to make prototype-based predictions more reliable?
reference_answer: It incorporates binary masks obtained automatically from a segmentation network and user-refined prototypes, guiding learned prototypes to correspond to relevant areas within the skin lesion while excluding confounding factors beyond its boundaries. Even without expert supervision, this yields superior performance and generalization compared to non-interpretable models.
gold_titles: XAI for Skin Cancer Detection with Prototypes and Non-Expert Supervision

question: How can generative diffusion bridges better model processes with memory and long-range temporal dependencies, and what tasks have been used to evaluate this approach?
reference_answer: The framework uses a Markovian approximation of fractional Brownian motion to enable tractable inference while retaining its non-Markovian properties, and supports both future-state prediction from paired data and unpaired data translation. It is evaluated on predicting future protein conformations and on unpaired image translation, outperforming Brownian baselines on both tasks.
gold_titles: Fractional Diffusion Bridge Models

question: When large language models are extended to tasks that jointly process visual and textual inputs, what difficulties arise, and which practical strategies are used to improve reasoning accuracy both during post-training and at inference time?
reference_answer: Extending LLM reasoning into multimodal contexts remains a significant challenge, since models must integrate visual and textual inputs, resolve conflicting information across modalities, and adopt advanced interpretative strategies. The survey formulates core reasoning challenges and opportunities, and highlights practical methods for post-training optimization and test-time inference, alongside methodologies for evaluating reasoning accuracy and coherence.
gold_titles: Why Reasoning Matters? A Survey of Advancements in Multimodal Reasoning (v1)

question: Why might a robot planner benefit more from forecasts of how a person's future movement affects its plan than from the most likely motion prediction?
reference_answer: At critical transition points, human-motion forecasts can have high errors that degrade downstream planning. ManiCast instead predicts motion in a way that captures its effect on the robot's plan cost, then supplies those forecasts to a model predictive control planner for collaborative manipulation.
gold_titles: ManiCast: Collaborative Manipulation with Cost-Aware Human Forecasting

question: How can dose prediction for radiotherapy be made more adaptable to different planners' institutional styles and organ trade-off priorities without being constrained by a single reference plan?
reference_answer: A generative model predicts 3D dose distributions from user-defined preference flavors, letting planners customize trade-offs between organs-at-risk and planning target volumes. Evaluations show it can surpass Varian RapidPlan in adaptability and plan quality in some scenarios.
gold_titles: Demo: Generative AI helps Radiotherapy Planning with User Preference

question: When checking the robustness of networks with smooth activations such as Sigmoid and Tanh through convex relaxation, how much better are the linear upper and lower bounds obtained by automatically searching for good parameters compared to the best previously reported bounds?
reference_answer: A straightforward parameter search, tuned to the verification task with state-of-the-art algorithm configuration techniques, improves the average global lower bound by 25% over the current state of the art on several commonly used local robustness verification benchmarks.
gold_titles: Automated Design of Linear Bounding Functions for Sigmoidal Nonlinearities in Neural Networks

question: How does MFSNN extract and integrate features from invasive BCI signals, and what learning strategy improves its cross-day decoding robustness?
reference_answer: MFSNN uses temporal convolutional networks and channel attention mechanisms to extract spatiotemporal features from raw data, then integrates these features through skip connections. It uses mini-batch supervised generalization learning to improve generalizability and robustness in cross-day signal decoding.
gold_titles: Multiscale fusion enhanced spiking neural network for invasive BCI neural signal decoding

question: How do the two works use LoRA to address different challenges, and what benefits do they report in their respective settings?
reference_answer: The federated fine-tuning work introduces RoLoRA, which applies alternating minimization to LoRA to improve robustness as fine-tuning parameters decrease and data heterogeneity increases, while retaining communication benefits. The crash-narrative work uses LoRA and BERT to inject task-specific knowledge into compact language models for inference-heavy extraction; its fine-tuned models outperform strong closed LLMs such as GPT-4o while using minimal training resources.
gold_titles: Robust Federated Finetuning of Foundation Models via Alternating Minimization of LoRA || Domain-Adapted Pre-trained Language Models for Implicit Information Extraction in Crash Narratives

question: How is knowledge distillation used in each work, and what distinct purpose does it serve in the respective pipelines?
reference_answer: In the first work, knowledge distillation is combined with Chain-of-Thought prompting to support the reasoning and training of an audio language model that corrects and re-synthesizes speech after an initial separation stage. In the second work, knowledge distillation uses NeRF-synthesized results as a teacher signal to guide the correct coloration of light segments in the faster Neural Light Dynamic Fields model. Thus, the former uses distillation to facilitate language-model reasoning and training for robust speech separation, while the latter uses it to transfer appearance or color information from a NeRF-based renderer into an efficient light-segment representation for 3D talking-head generation.
gold_titles: SepALM: Audio Language Models Are Error Correctors for Robust Speech Separation || NLDF: Neural Light Dynamic Fields for Efficient 3D Talking Head Generation

question: How do the two studies use GPT-2 activations to investigate its internal behavior, and what distinct findings do they report?
reference_answer: One study examines neuron activations associated with literary versus rigid prose and uses ablation to show that removing 50 highly discriminative neurons improves literary-style metrics by 25.7%, cautioning that correlation does not imply causal necessity. The other visualizes layerwise latent states with PCA and UMAP, reporting a separation between attention and MLP outputs, high norms at the initial sequence position, and a helical structure in GPT-2 positional embeddings.
gold_titles: Atomic Literary Styling: Mechanistic Manipulation of Prose Generation in Neural Language Models || Visualizing LLM Latent Space Geometry Through Dimensionality Reduction

question: Two studies use LSTMs in very different settings: one applies the network to predict real-time go-around probability for arriving aircraft near JFK and then embeds the pre-trained models in a live data-streaming tool, while the other deliberately constructs leaky and clean LSTM forecasting pipelines to test how validation design distorts measured performance. How does each study handle the temporal structure of its data, and which validation configuration does the leakage analysis find most vulnerable, with what reported penalty?
reference_answer: In the aviation application, the LSTM predicts the real-time go-around probability of an arrival flight within 10 nm of JFK's landing threshold, the resulting pre-trained models are integrated with real-time data streaming into a web-based interface for flight crews and line personnel, and in-trail spacing plus simultaneous runway operation emerge as the top factors behind go-arounds. In the methodological study, LSTM forecasting pipelines are built leaky (input-output sequences constructed before dataset partitioning) versus clean (temporal separation enforced before sequence construction), and 10-fold cross-validation is the most vulnerable setup with RMSE Gain of up to 20.5% at extended lag steps, whereas 2-way and 3-way splits stay robust at typically below 5%, with smaller input windows and longer lags increasing leakage risk. Together they indicate that an LSTM's value in a live, safety-critical deployment hinges as much on how temporally ordered data are split and validated as on the network architecture itself.
gold_titles: Real-Time Go-Around Prediction: A case study of JFK airport || Hidden Leaks in Time Series Forecasting: How Data Leakage Affects LSTM Evaluation Across Configurations and Validation Strategies

question: How does DeepSeek-R1 contribute differently to improving reasoning in dual-agent causal debate versus internal-state probing for test-time scaling, and what results support each approach?
reference_answer: In dual-agent causal debate, DeepSeek-R1 serves as a debater that critiques and revises causal reasoning alongside another agent; its CLadder overall accuracy increases from 78.03% to 87.45%, and counterfactual accuracy rises from 67.94% to 80.04%. In internal-state probing, DeepSeek-R1 is an example of a larger LLM that can provide training annotations for a lightweight probe estimating reasoning-step credibility, although self-supervised annotation is also possible. Across mathematics, planning, and general knowledge question answering, probes with fewer than 10 million parameters match or exceed process reward models up to 810 times larger.
gold_titles: CRAwDAD: Causal Reasoning Augmentation with Dual-Agent Debate || ReProbe: Efficient Test-Time Scaling of Multi-Step Reasoning by Probing Internal States of Large Language Models

question: How does each work employ a hybrid approach combining established theoretical or analytical methods with modern computational tools to overcome limitations in its respective domain?
reference_answer: The first work combines constructive alignment theory and Bloom's taxonomy with AI tools to redesign educational assessment, while the second combines machine-learning regression with an SMT-solver and computer algebra system to solve recurrence relations. Both use a hybrid strategy: one integrates pedagogical theory with AI capabilities to align learning objectives and assessment, and the other integrates symbolic and statistical techniques to overcome the limitations of existing recurrence solvers in cost analysis.
gold_titles: The Impact of AI on Educational Assessment: A Framework for Constructive Alignment || A Machine Learning-based Approach for Solving Recurrence Relations and its use in Cost Analysis of Logic Programs

question: How is the Gemma2 model put to work in these two studies, and what does each study conclude about Gemma2's effectiveness in the role it is given there?
reference_answer: In the retrieval evaluation, Gemma2 is one of seven off-the-shelf document retrieval models (with Splade, Plaid, Plaid-X, SimCSE, Contriever and OpenAI ADA) benchmarked on the Czech dataset DaReCzech, where it achieved the highest precision and recall while Contriever performed poorly and SPLADE and PLAID offered a better balance of efficiency and performance. In the continual-learning study, Gemma2's full parameter set is autoregressively pretrained on the first 10% of the Lithuanian component of CulturaX, with Elastic Weight Consolidation based on Fisher information from MMLU to prevent catastrophic forgetting, so the adapted model improved or maintained both linguistic fluency (perplexity) and domain knowledge (ARC-Easy, Belebele, GSM8K, HellaSwag, MMLU, TruthfulQA, Winogrande) in English and Lithuanian. Together they show Gemma2 serving as a strong out-of-the-box retrieval engine for Czech in one case and as an efficiently adaptable general-purpose base model for an under-represented language in the other.
gold_titles: A Comparative Study of Text Retrieval Models on DaReCzech || Full-Parameter Continual Pretraining of Gemma2: Insights into Fluency and Domain Knowledge

question: How do these works address different challenges involving visual inputs, and what does each do to improve model performance or efficiency?
reference_answer: CARES predicts the minimal sufficient image resolution for a query, preserving a target VLM’s task performance while reducing compute by up to 80%. LogiDynamics uses a controlled analogical reasoning environment across textual, visual, and symbolic modalities to compare inference strategies, finding that System 2 generally excels on visual and symbolic tasks and that hypothesis selection and iterative refinement can strengthen reasoning.
gold_titles: CARES: Context-Aware Resolution Selector for VLMs || LogiDynamics: Unraveling the Dynamics of Inductive, Abductive and Deductive Logical Inferences in LLM Reasoning

question: How does Gemma's role differ between research on personalized offensiveness detection in political tweets and research on Egyptian Arabic-English code-switched language processing, and what main findings does each report?
reference_answer: In offensiveness detection, Gemma is among the LLMs evaluated on political tweets across English, Polish, and Russian using different political personas; the study finds that larger models with explicit reasoning are more consistent and sensitive to ideological and cultural variation. In code-switched Egyptian Arabic-English processing, Gemma and Llama are used for machine translation, alongside Whisper-based speech recognition in a consecutive speech-to-text translation system; the reported translation improvements over the state of the art are 56% for English and 9.3% for Arabic.
gold_titles: Language, Culture, and Ideology: Personalizing Offensiveness Detection in Political Tweets with Reasoning LLMs || ArzEn-LLM: Code-Switched Egyptian Arabic-English Translation and Speech Recognition Using LLMs

question: How do the two works use different approaches to improve inference or prediction under distributional change?
reference_answer: The stationary diffusion approach models systems through SDEs whose stationary densities represent behavior under interventions, and it can generalize to unseen interventions without requiring causal graphs. The SDM approach modifies softmax with similarity and distance-to-training-distribution awareness, improving selective-classification robustness to covariate shifts and out-of-distribution inputs.
gold_titles: Causal Modeling with Stationary Diffusions || Similarity-Distance-Magnitude Activations

question: How does each work's use of direct preference optimization differ in purpose and scope, and what specific limitation does the multimodal approach aim to correct?
reference_answer: One work applies standard DPO as the final alignment stage after supervised fine-tuning for its openly released 1.8B chat models, without modifying the DPO method itself. The other proposes mDPO, a multimodal variant that optimizes image preferences and adds a reward anchor to address the unconditional preference problem, where models overlook the image condition and chosen responses can lose likelihood.
gold_titles: H2O-Danube-1.8B Technical Report || mDPO: Conditional Preference Optimization for Multimodal Large Language Models

question: Two different studies place GPT-4o at the center of their evaluation — one as the model whose prompting/fine-tuning strategy is being optimized for a structured-data extraction task, the other as one of several frontier generators inside a retrieval-augmented pipeline. In each case, what role does GPT-4o play, which configuration performed best for it, and what does each study conclude about whether added prompting effort or raw visual evidence actually pays off?
reference_answer: In the product attribute-value extraction work, GPT-4o was the model under study, and the strongest setup was fine-tuning when development data was available, since error-based prompt rewriting and self-correction did not significantly improve extraction performance while substantially inflating token/processing costs (with fine-tuning ramp-up amortized as more product descriptions are added). In the biomedical multi-modal RAG case study, GPT-4o was one of the frontier proprietary generators being compared across augmentation strategies, where converting figures/tables to text worked best (0.808 average accuracy) ahead of text RAG (0.782) and OCR-free visual retrieval (0.745), with within-model differences small. Taken together, the two findings indicate that GPT-4o performs best when the surrounding pipeline does the interpretive lifting for it — through task-specific fine-tuning or through pre-converting visual evidence into text — rather than through extra self-refinement passes or handing the model page images to interpret directly.
gold_titles: Self-Refinement Strategies for LLM-based Product Attribute Value Extraction || Exploration of Augmentation Strategies in Multi-modal Retrieval-Augmented Generation for the Biomedical Domain: A Case Study Evaluating Question Answering in Glycobiology

question: How does WordNet support text representations in evolutionary aerodynamic vehicle design optimization versus crossmodal knowledge distillation for image classification, and what limitations or benefits do the two approaches report?
reference_answer: In aerodynamic vehicle design optimization, WordNet samples populate a prompt-template-based bag-of-words representation evaluated within an automated evolutionary framework using Shap-E; the findings emphasize keeping generated designs within the intended object class and improving the causal relationship between prompt variations and 3D design changes. In image classification, semantically richer WordNet expansions replace exact class names in learnable text embeddings combined with CLIP image embeddings under a hierarchical loss, mitigating label leakage and improving student performance while encouraging reliance on visual features rather than textual shortcuts.
gold_titles: Large Language and Text-to-3D Models for Engineering Design Optimization || Crossmodal Knowledge Distillation with WordNet-Relaxed Text Embeddings for Robust Image Classification

question: How does each work use natural language processing in its overall pipeline, and what distinct end goal does that usage serve?
reference_answer: One work uses NLP together with knowledge graphs to automate the extraction, representation, and retrieval of Function Behaviour-Structure knowledge from legacy structured product data lacking contextual information. The other applies NLP techniques during dataset pre-processing to train machine learning and deep-learning models that predict suitable career paths for Computer Science and Software Engineering students.
gold_titles: Automated Extraction and Creation of FBS Design Reasoning Knowledge Graphs from Structured Data in Product Catalogues Lacking Contextual Information || Unlocking Futures: A Natural Language Driven Career Prediction System for Computer Science and Software Engineering Students

question: How is BERT used differently in translating natural-language requests into data visualizations versus assigning publication types to MEDLINE citations, and what alternative models or classifier designs are explored in each setting?
reference_answer: For data visualization, BERT serves as an encoder in sequence-to-sequence Transformer architectures that translate natural-language queries into simplified Vega Zero commands, with available T5 sequence-to-sequence models applied for comparison. For MEDLINE indexing, pre-trained BERT and DistilBERT predict MeSH Publication Types from citation metadata through monolithic multi-label classifiers and binary classifier ensembles, with results indicating potential improvements in tagging accuracy.
gold_titles: Natural Language Models for Data Visualization Utilizing nvBench Dataset || Enhancing Automatic PT Tagging for MEDLINE Citations Using Transformer-Based Models

question: How do the two studies use convolutional neural networks in different biomedical classification settings, and what does each study show about improving model reliability or interpretability?
reference_answer: The biomedical image study evaluates CNNs alongside other architectures for whole-slide image classification and finds that automatic labels can perform comparably to manual labels when label noise is limited, with SKET-generated labels having 2–5% noise. The cough-analysis study uses a CNN to process spectrograms, then applies occlusion maps and spectral analysis to reveal disease-related acoustic patterns, including greater variability for COPD patients in relevant spectral regions.
gold_titles: Automatic Labels are as Effective as Manual Labels in Biomedical Images Classification with Deep Learning || XAI-Driven Spectral Analysis of Cough Sounds for Respiratory Disease Characterization

question: How do deita and H2O-Danube differ in their use of Mistral and their approaches to efficient language-model development, and what alignment stages do they share?
reference_answer: deita fine-tunes LLaMA and Mistral models using instruction data automatically selected based on complexity, quality, and diversity, matching or exceeding baseline alignment performance with only 6K supervised fine-tuning samples. H2O-Danube instead follows core principles of LLaMA 2 and Mistral to develop competitive 1.8B-parameter models, with the initial model trained on 1T tokens and its improved version on an additional 2T tokens. Both use supervised fine-tuning followed by direct preference optimization for aligned or chat models.
gold_titles: What Makes Good Data for Alignment? A Comprehensive Study of Automatic Data Selection in Instruction Tuning || H2O-Danube-1.8B Technical Report

question: How does each work relate in-context learning to the capabilities it seeks to improve, and what distinct role does it assign to demonstrations or inference strategies?
reference_answer: One work uses in-context learning as a training-free replacement for supervised parameter updating in soft sensing, feeding structured demonstrations to a large language model to gain predictive performance, robustness, and self-explaining uncertainty estimates. The other studies how inductive versus abductive/deductive inference strategies shape LLM reasoning, finding that System 2 pipelines generally excel on harder visual and symbolic tasks while System 1 can win on free-text rule execution, and it shows that hypothesis selection and iterative refinement scale these capabilities.
gold_titles: A Soft Sensor Method with Uncertainty-Awareness and Self-Explanation Based on Large Language Models Enhanced by Domain Knowledge Retrieval || LogiDynamics: Unraveling the Dynamics of Inductive, Abductive and Deductive Logical Inferences in LLM Reasoning

question: In both studies Qwen3 is evaluated alongside other large language models, but in very different settings: once as a debating agent in a dual-agent framework for causal inference on the CLadder benchmark, and once as one of several models judging offensiveness in political tweets from varied ideological personas in English, Polish, and Russian. What role does Qwen3 play in each setting, and what do the reported results say about how much its performance depends on explicit reasoning ability versus collaboration with another model?
reference_answer: In the causal reasoning study, Qwen3 serves as a debater agent whose CLadder accuracy rises from 84.16% to 89.41% overall (and from 71.53% to 80.35% on counterfactual questions) when it debates a second model, indicating that even a strong model benefits from structured collaboration with a weaker partner. In the offensiveness study, Qwen3 is simply one of several evaluated LLMs (alongside DeepSeek-R1, o4-mini, GPT-4.1-mini, Gemma, and Mistral) prompted to judge tweets from far-right, conservative, centrist, and progressive viewpoints across three languages, where explicit reasoning models such as DeepSeek-R1 and o4-mini were the most consistent and sensitive to ideological and cultural variation. Taken together, the results suggest that inherent reasoning capability drives consistent, persona-sensitive judgments, while adding a debate partner with an adversarial perspective further strengthens an already capable model like Qwen3 on multi-step causal tasks.
gold_titles: CRAwDAD: Causal Reasoning Augmentation with Dual-Agent Debate || Language, Culture, and Ideology: Personalizing Offensiveness Detection in Political Tweets with Reasoning LLMs

question: How do these two works use retrieval-augmented generation for different user-facing goals, and what does each add beyond a basic RAG pipeline?
reference_answer: ARAG targets personalized recommendations, adding four specialized agents to interpret long-term and session preferences, assess candidate relevance, summarize findings, and rank items; it reports gains over standard RAG and recency-based baselines. RiverEcho targets cultural education, using a curated ancient Yellow River knowledge dataset and a voice-driven talking-head digital human to provide more professional and informative explanations.
gold_titles: ARAG: Agentic Retrieval Augmented Generation for Personalized Recommendation || RiverEcho: Real-Time Interactive Digital System for Ancient Yellow River Culture

question: How do two approaches involving deep ensembles differ in how they represent and manage uncertainty: one for classification and out-of-distribution detection, and the other for medical large language models?
reference_answer: The classification approach wraps predictions from deep ensembles or Bayesian neural networks in class-wise lower and upper probability bounds that define a credal set, explicitly acknowledging epistemic uncertainty from a limited collection of predictive distributions; it reports improved out-of-distribution uncertainty estimation and lower calibration error on corrupted data. The medical LLM approach combines deep ensembles, Bayesian inference, and Monte Carlo dropout with linguistic analysis of predictive and semantic entropy to manage both epistemic and aleatoric uncertainties, incorporating surrogate modeling, dynamic calibration, and interpretable uncertainty maps and confidence metrics.
gold_titles: Credal Wrapper of Model Averaging for Uncertainty Estimation in Classification || The challenge of uncertainty quantification of large language models in medicine

question: How does each work use an attention mechanism within its predictive model, and what specific modeling challenge is attention intended to address in each case?
reference_answer: One work combines radial basis function layers with attention to capture nonlinear inter-dependencies in the temporal evolution of a chaotic physical attractor for trajectory prediction. The other adds attention to CNNs processing 3D brain SPECT images as sequences of 2D slices, so slices can be weighted by their varying importance in multiclass Parkinson's disease stage prediction.
gold_titles: A Multi-Branched Radial Basis Network Approach to Predicting Complex Chaotic Behaviours || Deep Convolutional Neural Networks on Multiclass Classification of Three-Dimensional Brain Images for Parkinson's Disease Stage Prediction

question: How do the works on automatic instruction-data selection and Egyptian Arabic-English code-switching use LLaMA for different goals, and what results do they report?
reference_answer: The data-selection work fine-tunes LLaMA and Mistral into deita models using instruction samples selected according to complexity, quality, and diversity, matching or exceeding leading open-source alignment models with only 6K supervised fine-tuning samples—over 10 times fewer than the baselines. The code-switching work uses LLaMA and Gemma for machine translation and Whisper for speech recognition within a consecutive speech-to-text translation system, reporting improvements over the state of the art of 56% for English translation and 9.3% for Arabic translation.
gold_titles: What Makes Good Data for Alignment? A Comprehensive Study of Automatic Data Selection in Instruction Tuning || ArzEn-LLM: Code-Switched Egyptian Arabic-English Translation and Speech Recognition Using LLMs

question: How do the two studies use Random Forest and boosting methods, and what does each report about their results?
reference_answer: The stock-market study compares Random Forest with Extreme Gradient Boosting to forecast US market crisis events from daily financial data and reports that Extreme Gradient Boosting performs best. The point-cloud study uses Random Forest and XGBoost to estimate point-level uncertainty from geometric features; both achieve mean ROC-AUC values above 0.87, with elevation variation, point density, and structural complexity among the most influential features.
gold_titles: CRISIS ALERT:Forecasting Stock Market Crisis Events Using Machine Learning Methods || Point-level Uncertainty Evaluation of Mobile Laser Scanning Point Clouds

question: How does the privacy-preserving approach to collaborative battery control differ from the private proxy oracle framework for convex optimization, and what main result does each report?
reference_answer: The battery-control work uses personalized federated reinforcement learning for energy management in building microgrids, reporting that Federated TRPO performs comparably to state-of-the-art federated RL methods without hyperparameter tuning; its abstract does not describe a private proxy oracle. The convex-optimization work explicitly studies a private proxy oracle that sends only private messages about minibatches of gradients and establishes dimension-dependent lower bounds on the oracle queries needed to achieve a target excess risk.
gold_titles: Generalising Battery Control in Net-Zero Buildings via Personalised Federated RL || On the Gradient Complexity of Private Optimization with Private Oracles

question: In what distinct roles is GPT-4 used to support expert work in the two studies, and how do their respective application domains and levels of autonomy differ?
reference_answer: In the neurological-disorder study, GPT-4 generates disease concepts that guide semantic patch weighting and graph-based prompting of a multimodal model for diagnosis. In the empirical legal study, GPT-4 directly collaborates with a legal expert to generate initial codes, classify facts descriptions, and discover themes in thematic analysis. Thus, the first uses GPT-4 indirectly to inform a downstream medical model, while the second uses it as an interactive analytical assistant whose outputs can be refined through expert feedback.
gold_titles: MMGPL: Multimodal Medical Data Analysis with Graph Prompt Learning || Using Large Language Models to Support Thematic Analysis in Empirical Legal Studies

question: How do the two works address different limitations in the use of SHAP explanations, and what does each contribute?
reference_answer: One work extends SHAP with an LLM that uses user-defined context to produce textual explanations; its healthcare case study found these were perceived as more understandable and contextually appropriate than visual-only outputs. The other provides a framework for generating and rigorously evaluating post-hoc explanation methods, including SHAP, with metrics such as faithfulness, sensitivity, and robustness across tabular and image data.
gold_titles: ContextualSHAP : Enhancing SHAP Explanations Through Contextual Language Generation || xai_evals : A Framework for Evaluating Post-Hoc Local Explanation Methods

question: How do the two federated learning approaches address different practical constraints, and what mechanism does each use to improve training outcomes?
reference_answer: For medical image segmentation with incomplete annotations, one approach treats missing or incorrect labels as noisy data, evaluates annotation completeness per client, and gives more influence to clients with comprehensive annotations while correcting incomplete ones. For satellite clusters with intermittent connectivity, the other uses coordinated inter-orbit and intra-orbit schedulers to time global updates and allocate local training time based on satellite availability.
gold_titles: FedIA: Federated Medical Image Segmentation with Heterogeneous Annotation Completeness || Scheduling for On-Board Federated Learning with Satellite Clusters

question: How do two approaches involving CLIP modify class-name-based text inputs to improve image recognition, and why does one avoid exact class names while the other replaces scientific names with common English names?
reference_answer: For crossmodal knowledge distillation, one approach combines CLIP image embeddings with learnable WordNet-relaxed text embeddings under a hierarchical loss, replacing exact class names with richer semantic expansions to mitigate label leakage and reduce textual shortcuts. For zero-shot species recognition, the other replaces scientific names with common English names that are more likely to occur in CLIP's training data, achieving 2–5 times higher accuracy on fine-grained species recognition benchmarks.
gold_titles: Crossmodal Knowledge Distillation with WordNet-Relaxed Text Embeddings for Robust Image Classification || Prompting Scientific Names for Zero-Shot Species Recognition

question: How does each work use variational inference to support its primary objective, and what distinct outputs or goals result from those uses?
reference_answer: One work applies Bayesian training via variational inference to quantify both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty in DeepONet-PINN models for solving PDEs and estimating their unknown parameters. The other uses variational inference to derive the evidence lower bound for a conditional generative diffusion model, enabling reconstruction of fine-grained channel fingerprints from coarse-grained observations.
gold_titles: Deep Operator Networks for Bayesian Parameter Estimation in PDEs || Channel Fingerprint Construction for Massive MIMO: A Deep Conditional Generative Approach

question: How do the two works use focal loss or federated learning to address different challenges, and what role does focal loss play in the calibration approach compared with the UAV spectrum-sensing approach?
reference_answer: The calibration approach uses a meta-learner to assign sample-wise gamma values for focal loss, with smooth expected calibration error guiding optimization toward unbiased, robust calibration. The UAV spectrum-sensing approach instead uses federated learning and SNR-weighted model aggregation to train a global sensing model across distributed UAVs; its abstract does not describe using focal loss.
gold_titles: Towards Unbiased Calibration using Meta-Regularization || Federated Learning for UAV-Based Spectrum Sensing: Enhancing Accuracy Through SNR-Weighted Model Aggregation

question: How do the two works use adaptive or specialized modeling to address different challenges, and what role do masked autoencoders play in the cloud-reconstruction approach?
reference_answer: MASS adapts the size of a mixture-of-experts pool when semantic drift indicates the experts cannot capture the data’s diversity, and adjusts routing according to token-level confidence. The cloud-reconstruction study uses masked autoencoders, including geospatially-aware SatMAE, for self-supervised learning on unlabeled satellite imagery before fine-tuning on paired images and cloud profiles.
gold_titles: How Many Experts Are Enough? Towards Optimal Semantic Specialization for Mixture-of-Experts || 3D Cloud reconstruction through geospatially-aware Masked Autoencoders

question: How does expected calibration error serve different roles in research on post-processing online predictors for decision-making and in knowledge graph-guided synthetic QA data generation, and what does each approach aim to achieve?
reference_answer: In the online prediction work, expected calibration error is a discontinuous calibration measure relevant to decision-making; adding differentially private noise to post-process a predictor with ε distance to calibration achieves an asymptotically optimal O(√ε) bound on ECE and Calibration Decision Loss. In GraphGen, expected calibration error instead identifies LLM knowledge gaps, guiding the generation of QA pairs targeting high-value, long-tail knowledge to improve synthetic data for supervised fine-tuning.
gold_titles: Smooth Calibration and Decision Making || GraphGen: Enhancing Supervised Fine-Tuning for LLMs with Knowledge-Driven Synthetic Data Generation

question: How do the two defenses differ in the signals they use to detect backdoors, and what kinds of difficult attacks or data conditions does each address?
reference_answer: One builds tubular neighborhoods around class-specific hidden-feature manifolds and flags inputs whose layerwise, locally adaptive ranking patterns depart from the expected tube-constrained behavior; it is designed to work even with very few clean examples. The other strengthens topological evolution tracking with label supervision and adaptive layer emphasis, targeting attacks that distort topological representations across layers, including subtle perturbations and cases where the representations are inseparable in topological space.
gold_titles: TED++: Submanifold-Aware Backdoor Detection via Layerwise Tubular-Neighbourhood Screening || TED-LaST: Towards Robust Backdoor Defense Against Adaptive Attacks

question: How does each work use UMAP to turn high-dimensional data into a visual or geometric representation, and what distinct analysis does each extract from the resulting low-dimensional structure?
reference_answer: One work applies PCA and UMAP to layerwise Transformer activations from GPT-2 and LLaMa, revealing geometric patterns such as separation between attention and MLP outputs, high-norm initial-position states, helical positional embeddings, and layerwise latent-state evolution. The other projects each unit's sensor degradation trajectory into a lower-dimensional space with UMAP and then clusters those trajectories to diagnose unknown failure modes, which feed a monotonic prognostic model that predicts failure-mode labels and remaining useful life.
gold_titles: Visualizing LLM Latent Space Geometry Through Dimensionality Reduction || Degradation Modeling and Prognostic Analysis Under Unknown Failure Modes

question: What distinct roles does ChatGPT play in these two lines of work, and how does each contribution differ in whether ChatGPT is the object of evaluation or the mechanism proposed for solving a problem?
reference_answer: In the group recommendation work, ChatGPT is cited as a modern generative AI assistant whose capabilities motivate reorienting group recommender systems so that group members converse in a chat while an AI-based group recommendation agent assists decision-making in an agentic way, with the aim of enabling more natural group decisions and wider real-world adoption. In the financial benchmarking work, ChatGPT is instead one of several systems (alongside Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini, and traditional machine-learning models) whose outputs are evaluated as sentiment analyzers on Microsoft earnings call transcripts, scored for accuracy and for how well their detected sentiment correlates with market sentiment and stock movements, with prompt engineering explored as an improvement. Thus one contribution harnesses ChatGPT's conversational capacity as a proposed system design, while the other empirically tests the reliability of ChatGPT on a specialized, high-stakes language task where hedged and ambiguous wording causes misinterpretation.
gold_titles: Rethinking Group Recommender Systems in the Era of Generative AI: From One-Shot Recommendations to Agentic Group Decision Support || Can AI Read Between The Lines? Benchmarking LLMs On Financial Nuance

question: How do experience replay and the kernel formulation of next-generation reservoir computing respectively improve computational efficiency in kernel ridge regression, and what additional benefit does each approach provide?
reference_answer: The experience replay approach uses a framework based on resampled U- and V-statistics to reduce kernel ridge regression's time cost from O(n^3) to as low as O(n^2), while also reducing variance. The next-generation reservoir computing approach encodes the method as kernel ridge regression, making training feasible with very large polynomial feature spaces; its extension to infinitely many covariates also removes dependence on choosing past lags and the number of polynomial covariates.
gold_titles: Variance Reduction via Resampling and Experience Replay || Infinite-dimensional next-generation reservoir computing

question: How does each work make use of its central computational method, and what distinct goal does that method serve in its application domain?
reference_answer: One work maps the Tsetlin Machine's learning automaton into a single Y-Flash memristive cell, using the device's conductance range to represent the automaton's range for in-memory, on-edge learning. The other applies topic modeling to task-oriented dialogue datasets to find topics similar to social-talk keywords, revealing naturally occurring chit-chat sequences.
gold_titles: In-Memory Learning Automata Architecture using Y-Flash Cell || Searching for Snippets of Open-Domain Dialogue in Task-Oriented Dialogue Datasets

question: How does each work respectively use a Vision Transformer, and what distinct data-related challenge does each address when applying this architecture?
reference_answer: One work uses a Vision Transformer to predict density heatmaps over time and total evacuation time directly from building floorplans, addressing limited public data by creating a large synthetic dataset through a parametric pipeline with a conventional simulator. The other evaluates a Vision Transformer among multiple architectures for classifying biomedical whole slide images, addressing the need for expert annotations by showing that automatic labels remain effective when their noise stays at or below about 10 percent.
gold_titles: Towards predicting Pedestrian Evacuation Time and Density from Floorplans using a Vision Transformer || Automatic Labels are as Effective as Manual Labels in Biomedical Images Classification with Deep Learning

question: Both works reuse ImageNet-pretrained convolutional networks but adapt them to very different data (3D brain SPECT images vs.2D dermoscopic skin images). How does each one transfer ImageNet knowledge to its task, what specific modifications (architectural, augmentation, or training-procedure changes) were needed, and what outcomes were reported?
reference_answer: In the brain-imaging work, ImageNet-pretrained 2D CNNs were fed entire 3D SPECT volumes as sequences of 2D slices whose outputs were averaged, and these outperformed 3D CNNs pretrained on Kinetics-400; the authors added a slice-level attention mechanism to weight slices differently and used cotraining with weight sharing across two hospitals' data sets, which improved performance when the cotraining data sets were sufficiently large. In the skin-disease work, ImageNet weights from VGG16 were retained while the top layers were replaced with fully connected layers and a final softmax to classify actinic keratosis and psoriasis, with rotation, shifting and zooming used for augmentation, yielding 90.67% accuracy. Thus one adapts ImageNet features slice-wise within a 3D pipeline with attention and multi-site cotraining, while the other fine-tunes a single 2D ImageNet backbone with augmented inputs and a new classification head.
gold_titles: Deep Convolutional Neural Networks on Multiclass Classification of Three-Dimensional Brain Images for Parkinson's Disease Stage Prediction || Skin Disease Detection and Classification of Actinic Keratosis and Psoriasis Utilizing Deep Transfer Learning
